scope: 1000 synthetic symbols through hquant_server's live Binance-compatible WebSocket and REST inputs on local macOS

issues.finding: The former replay benchmark parses a file and waits for each shard completion before reading the next record. Its QPS includes this artificial round trip and does not measure the live feed.
issues.action: Added an independent paced WebSocket/REST sender. The old benchmark is labeled as a serial replay diagnostic.

issues.finding: Replay symbols such as STRESS_SIM_0001 contain underscores, while the live Binance input permits only uppercase letters and digits.
issues.action: The sender and live config map these to STRESSSIM0001 and equivalent names; fixture identities and per-symbol expectations remain paired.

issues.finding: Python monotonic_ns and C++ steady_clock exposed different epochs on this macOS host, making initial cross-process latency values invalid.
issues.action: The control clock endpoint calibrates the offset using the lowest-round-trip sample and checks drift after every run. Final run drift was within 6 microseconds.

issues.finding: The first 180-second SSE-pattern run filled the fixed 8192-record history queue: 180000 records attempted, 164676 written, 15324 dropped, 7645 gap rows, 402 shards affected. The benchmark failed correctness.
issues.cause: Synchronized refresh across 1000 shards produces short bursts of order commands, reports, and balance rows; the single SQLite writer cannot drain the fixed queue during the burst.
issues.action: History queue capacity now scales to max(8192, 64 * shard_count). The rerun wrote all 166000 records, had zero gaps, and reached a queue peak of 12810. This capacity handles the tested cases; a larger or sustained burst can still overflow the finite queue.

issues.finding: At 4x rate with 1000 simultaneous first depth updates and REST snapshots inside timing, sender schedule p99 was 28.166 ms and wire-to-market p99 was 61.440 ms; the final state was correct.
issues.action: Added a separate first-depth warmup option. At 4x after all 1000 books became Live, 299000 timed frames were sent in 7.500 seconds; sender schedule p99 was 0.051 ms and wire-to-market p99 was 0.050 ms.

issues.finding: macOS sample collected CPU stacks during the stress run but raised wire-to-market p99 to 57.148 ms, versus 0.050 ms in the unprofiled 10k/s run.
issues.action: Use sampled runs only for stack attribution; report latency and QPS from separate unprofiled runs.

issues.finding: Bazel printed Build completed successfully and produced hquant_server, then exited with code 37 because sysctl was denied during its own process teardown in the sandbox.
issues.action: Verified the linked binary exists and ran the seven existing end-to-end tests plus the live cases against it; this is a build-tool exit issue rather than a compile failure.

measurement_notes: Latency distributions on the receiver sample one in ten WebSocket messages per shard; counters, final depth, per-message digests, history sequence, and ledger checks cover all events.
Wire-to-market ends when the market and paper strategy callbacks finish. SQLite persistence is asynchronous and is reported separately for history records.

NYSE and SSE are synthetic traffic patterns carried through the existing Binance-compatible feed, not native exchange protocols. Tests use local unencrypted sockets and do not include WAN or TLS costs.
